name: QuantMoE-Bench: Examining Post-Training Quantization for Mixture-of-Experts
problem: MoE quantization is done at one uniform precision for the whole model, which is wrong because MoE's routing gives its experts structurally different activation statistics.
mechanism: A benchmark plus a structural observation rather than a new algorithm: because shared experts are accessed by EVERY token while token-conditioned experts are selectively activated, the two groups have very different quantization sensitivity and should not share a bit width. The paper measures a fine-grained, structure-aware precision assignment for MoE and shows uniform-precision PTQ is leaving quality on the table.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): existing methods 'adopt a fixed quantization precision for the entire MoE model', which 'can lead to suboptimal performance, without considering the inherent sparse structure'; the shared-expert vs token-conditioned-expert asymmetry implies different quantization requirements. NO compression ratio paired with a quality delta appears in the abstract - this is an evaluation/diagnostic contribution, so speedup_reported stays null rather than inventing a compression claim.
